title: How would you estimate how much bottled water the UK drinks each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many litres of bottled water does the UK drink each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A simple per-person estimate, with a useful sanity check against other countries' habits. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many litres of bottled water does the UK drink each year?

The approach

People × litres each per year.

Tip: Before giving the answer, check it from a second direction. It is the step most candidates skip.

Step by step

  1. People in the UK: 68M
  2. × 40 litres each per year (under a litre a week)

That gives about 2.72B litres a year.

Does it make sense?

Southern European countries drink several times more per person, which fits UK tap-water habits.

Real-world check

The UK population was about 69.3 million at mid-2024 (ONS). This example rounds to 68 million, which is fine: in an interview, any sensible round number is accepted as long as you say it.

Source: ONS: UK population estimates, mid-2024.

Use two segments to test the average

The original formula assumes 40 litres per person per year. A segmented approach might assume 30% of residents drink 100 litres of purchased bottled water annually while 70% drink 15 litres. Weighted average consumption is 40.5 litres per person, remarkably close to the shortcut. At 68 million residents, that implies approximately 2.75 billion litres.

Those are practice assumptions, not survey results. The exercise shows what a single per-person average conceals: some consumers buy bottled water daily while others rely on tap water. Tourism and on-the-go purchasing can also matter if the scope is water sold within the UK, rather than water consumed by UK residents.

To estimate retail market value, multiply by a price per litre, not a bottle price. A 500 ml bottle and a two-litre supermarket bottle have different prices per litre and different channels.
